issues.legal_issue: A claim or question arising under the rent-control scheme may be heard by the designated special court even when the parties do not have a landlord–tenant relationship.
material_facts: The plaintiff advanced a construction loan in expectation of receiving a tenancy in the building, but the premises were never let to him.
The plaintiff sued to recover the loan and enforce the charge, and the purchasers of the building disputed the special court’s jurisdiction.
The suit concerned a transaction permitted by the rent-control scheme.
issues.conclusion: A landlord–tenant relationship is not required for the special court to hear claims or questions arising under the Act; that requirement applies to the specified category of suits concerning rent or possession, not to every matter within the court’s jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 gives the designated court jurisdiction over claims or questions arising out of the Act or its provisions, without requiring a landlord–tenant relationship for every such claim. Section 18(2) also recognizes recovery rights in favour of “any person.” Importers and Manufacturers Ltd. v. Pheroze Framrose Taraporewala was applied; Shivaling Gangadhar v. Navnitlal Amritlal, Bishan v. Maharashtra W. & G. Co., and Bombay Grain Dealers v. Lakhmichand were considered and did not establish a universal landlord–tenant prerequisite.

predicates.rental_control_claim_or_question: The proceeding concerns a claim or question arising from rights or arrangements governed by the rent-control scheme.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship: The parties to the proceeding have a landlord–tenant relationship.
predicates.special_court_has_jurisdiction: The designated special court has jurisdiction to hear and decide the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a claim or question governed by the rent-control scheme, the designated special court has jurisdiction even if the parties are not landlord and tenant.

issues.legal_issue: A claim to enforce a construction-loan charge under an agreement permitted by the rent-control scheme arises under that scheme even though the agreement supplies the immediate cause of action.
material_facts: The plaintiff advanced money to finance construction of a building on the owners’ land.

The loan agreement was in writing and registered, required the intended premises to be let to the lender, provided for interest and repayment, secured the loan against the building and the owners’ interest in the land, and limited use of the loan to construction.
The plaintiff sought recovery of the loan and enforcement of the charge after the premises were not let to him; the owners later sold the property to the appellants.
Deciding the claim required consideration of whether the transaction was permitted and protected by the rent-control scheme and what relief followed from it.
issues.conclusion: The legality, validity, binding effect, and enforcement of the charge, and the relief sought on it, were claims or questions arising out of the Act and could be dealt with only by the special court.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18(3) and 28(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging Houses Rates Control Act, 1947 permit the specified construction-loan arrangement and assign claims or questions arising from the Act to the designated court. The agreement was a method contemplated by section 18(3); the fact that it furnished the cause of action did not make the dispute merely contractual. Union of India v. S.T. & C. Co. was followed and applied for the approach to whether a claim arises out of an instrument: whether recourse to the governing arrangement is necessary to decide the dispute. Importers and Manufacturers Ltd. v. Pheroze Framrose Taraporewala was also applied.

rule.if: construction_loan_recovery_proceeding and loan_financed_building_construction and agreement_written_and_registered and agreement_required_occupation_and_provided_interest_repayment_and_security and agreement_limited_loan_to_construction and claim_requires_deciding_agreement_legality_or_enforcement

predicates.construction_loan_recovery_proceeding: The proceeding seeks recovery of a loan advanced to finance construction and enforcement of security for that loan.
predicates.loan_financed_building_construction: The money was advanced to finance construction of a building on land held by the borrower.
predicates.agreement_written_and_registered: The parties recorded the financing arrangement in a written agreement and registered it.
predicates.agreement_required_occupation_and_provid: The agreement provided for occupation of premises by the lender and addressed interest, repayment, and security over the building and the borrower’s interest in the land.
predicates.agreement_limited_loan_to_construction: The agreement required the loan to be used for construction of the building.
predicates.claim_requires_deciding_agreement_legali: Deciding the claim requires determining the validity, binding effect, or enforcement of the financing arrangement.
predicates.special_court_has_exclusive_jurisdiction: Only the designated special court has jurisdiction to decide the claim.

issues.definition: When a construction-loan recovery proceeding rests on a written and registered construction-financing arrangement with the stated occupation, payment, security, and use terms, and deciding the claim requires determining the arrangement’s legality or enforcement, the designated special court has exclusive jurisdiction.
